one_line: A relatable complaint to camera in the first 3 seconds, then the product enters as the fix.

q1_hook.what: 0:00 eye-level medium shot: a girl about 8 to 10 at a desk with a squared notebook, facing the lens. Voice and word-by-word text: "אם יש משהו שאני ממש לא אוהבת זה שיעורי בית בחשבון". No product yet.
q1_hook.why: A familiar homework complaint, acted large and said to the lens, is spoken and written together (H4, H6, F6). It opens on the problem with no intro (H1). The joke comes from a real kid moment (K3). But the product is missing until 0:09, so the value is unclear for 12 s (H2).

beats.what: Girl complains to the lens with big gestures; word-by-word text of the line
beats.why: The problem, acted, in the first seconds

beats.what: She slumps over her notebook, head on hand, writing
beats.why: Shows the boredom instead of saying it

beats.what: A boy joins: "נו באמת זה עדיין חשבון"; a "חשבון בכיף" box on the table from 0:09
beats.why: A second voice and the product arrive together

beats.what: Top-down: coloured cards, box, marker, hourglass; "כרטיסיות חשבון מחיקות שיגרמו לילדים לאהוב לפתור"
beats.why: Names the product and its promise

beats.what: Both children race the hourglass, writing answers on cards; banners "אפשר לשחק ביחיד", "או להתחרות בזוג"
beats.why: Shows the game mechanic and two ways to play

beats.what: Close cutaway of the hourglass and scattered cards
They bicker and solve cards: "תעזור לי כמה זה"; "ניצחתי!!" at 0:38
Laughing: "את עדיין שונאת חשבון", "כן אבל את זה"
beats.why: The girl's turn from hating maths pays off the hook

beats.what: Box front close up, then box, cards, hourglass; "ללמוד בלי באמת להרגיש שלומדים מבית פלפוט"

q2_flow.interaction_prompts: None asked. The caption opens with a yes/no pitch question ("מחפשים דרך מקורית ומעניינת שהילדים יאהבו לפתור תרגילים?"), not a comment prompt.
q2_flow.why: A character who hates maths, a turn when the box arrives, and a win and laugh at 0:38 make a mini story (K2, H5). Product facts ride inside banter (R3). The payoff comes near the end (R4). The 0:16 to 0:27 shot is static for 11 s, held only by the children's action (R1).

q3_cta.what: None. The video ends on a tagline card, "חשבון בכיף ללמוד בלי באמת להרגיש שלומדים מבית פלפוט" (0:45 to 0:46). The caption has no link, code, price or where to buy, only "בשיתוף @palphot".
q3_cta.why: No ask keeps the sell light and names a benefit (C7). The cost is a dead end: a parent who wants the kit has no next step, no comment prompt, and the skit has no send ask though a parent might send it to a friend (R5, C4).

q4_shown.what: Two children at a home table; the "חשבון בכיף" box (36 cards) on the table from 0:09; top-down cards, marker, hourglass 0:11 to 0:16; the children writing answers and racing the hourglass 0:16 to 0:41; box front legible 0:43 to 0:45. No price, no adult.
q4_shown.why: The children's laughter and the win show the game being fun, which is the promise (K8). The box is first seen at 0:09, past the 2 s mark (S1), and named at 0:12 and 0:46 (H3). The proof is performed, not a parent's verdict (S6). Children's faces are shown, which LumeBook's own Reels avoid (S5).

q5_edit.what: 13 shots in 47 s, about 3.6 s each. Mostly static medium shots; a handheld top-down product shot 0:12 to 0:16; an hourglass cutaway at 0:28; the longest shot is 11.5 s (0:16 to 0:27). Word-by-word subtitles; hard cut to box close-ups at 0:43.
q5_edit.why: The girl's gestures give movement before the first cut at 3.8 s (E1). Cuts come at a moderate pace within one scene (E2). Word-by-word subtitles synced to the speech suit sound off and on (E4). It ends on the box with no tail (E8).

q6_topic.what: A sibling skit: a girl who hates maths homework turns it into a timed card game with her brother; serves parents of school-age children who resist maths practice.
q6_topic.why: The humour comes from a real homework moment (K3) and a real parent concern (K6). It builds to a win and laughter, a high-arousal positive peak (K1). The promise "שיגרמו לילדים לאהוב לפתור" is strong, shown only as a skit (K4).

q7_filmed.what: Phone propped at eye level at a home table, static medium two-shots, even daylight, a plain wall behind; the girl speaks to the lens in the opening; one handheld top-down shot of the cards; a close-up of the hourglass; a close-up of the box front.
q7_filmed.why: Direct address in the opening speaks to the viewer (F6). Home and phone footage look native, sharp and steady (H8, F7). The top-down shot and box close-up fill the frame so the cards and box text read (F5, F4).

q8_text.on_screen: White bold word-by-word subtitles with a dark outline, low in the frame (about 75 to 80% down): "אם יש משהו שאני ממש לא אוהבת זה שיעורי בית בחשבון" (0:00), "כרטיסיות חשבון מחיקות שיגרמו לילדים לאהוב לפתור" (0:13), "ניצחתי!!" (0:38). White top banners: "אפשר לשחק ביחיד" (0:16), "או להתחרות בזוג" (0:24). End: "חשבון בכיף ללמוד בלי באמת להרגיש שלומדים מבית פלפוט".
q8_text.caption: "מחפשים דרך מקורית ומעניינת שהילדים יאהבו לפתור תרגילים?". About 40 words: a yes/no question, a product line, kit contents, a confidence claim, "בשיתוף @palphot", then 5 hashtags. No link, no price.
q8_text.why: A text line in the first second states the problem (T3), and the burned-in speech works muted (T1). Both the subtitles and the top banners sit outside the safe zone (T4). The caption's first line is a keyword question, with 5 specific hashtags (T7). The partner line is mid-caption, no paid label (T8).

weak_points: The product shows at 0:09; no ask, price or place to buy; subtitles and banners outside the safe zone; staged acting; a strong promise; children's faces on screen, which LumeBook should avoid.
lumebook_takeaway: Open on a relatable one-line problem as text over the book on a desk, then show the book in use top-down; end on a clear title close-up.
not_verified: Price and where it is sold. Whether the children are the creator's own. Music. Corrections to coded file: the top banner reads "אפשר לשחק ביחיד", not "ביחד"; the faces on camera are children's, not "other adult". The machine transcript is garbled after 0:20, so I quoted the burned-in subtitles.
